haiku-low.q1: Keys load at process start, in main, before the HTTP server listens. So /healthz cannot pass until the load succeeds.
haiku-low.q2: It retries the whole load 3 times, 2 seconds apart, then logs the error (names only) and exits non-zero. It never becomes ready, the rollout halts, and old pods keep serving.
haiku-low.q3: A background timer re-reads all three secrets every 5 minutes and swaps in any changed (value, version) pair atomically. If the read fails, it keeps the last good values, logs a warning, and retries at the next tick.
haiku-low.q4: Inside each process's in-memory cache as {name: (value, version_id)}. Values must never be written to disk, environment variables, or logs.
haiku-low.q5: orders-api-prod can read orders-api/prod/* only. The security on-call is the only writer. Engineers have no access to prod.
haiku-low.q6: Old values remain in git history, which is not being rewritten, so they count as leaked. They are made harmless by rotating each key and revoking the old one at the provider.
haiku-low.q7: Every outgoing provider call runs secrets.get(name) and puts that value in the Authorization header. Clients keep no copy, so the refreshed key is used from the next request.
haiku-low.q8: The team checks /healthz on every pod and confirms all 4 show the new version id, waiting up to 10 minutes. Only then does the security on-call revoke the old key.
haiku-low.q9: Set store access, then copy keys into the store, then ship the code change that reads from the store and removes the keys from the committed file in one merge, then rotate keys at providers.
haiku-low.q10: From the secret store's orders-api/dev/* secrets, using the developer's own login. make run sets APP_ENV=dev.
haiku-low.q11: It does not start with a partial set. It retries the whole load 3 times, 2 seconds apart, then exits non-zero and never becomes ready.
haiku-low.q12: Not decided. Scheduled rotation is an open question for security, and this plan covers only the one-time rotation in step 5.

sonnet.q1: Keys are loaded at startup in main before the HTTP server starts listening, so /healthz (readiness) cannot pass until the load succeeds.
sonnet.q2: It retries the whole load 3 times, 2 seconds apart, then logs the error (names only) and exits non-zero. It never becomes ready, so the rollout halts and the old pods keep serving; live traffic is unaffected.
sonnet.q3: A background timer re-reads all three secrets every 5 minutes; if a version id changed, the new (value, version_id) pair replaces the old cache entry in one assignment. If the read fails, it keeps the last good value for any secret it couldn't read, updates the others, logs a warning (name and error, no value), retries at the next tick, and the app stays running and ready.
sonnet.q4: Held in an in-memory cache in each process: {name: (value, version_id)}. They must never be written to disk, environment variables or logs.
sonnet.q5: Read: orders-api-prod (read-only, only orders-api/prod/*). Write: only the security on-call. Engineers have no access to prod.
sonnet.q6: Old values remain in git history, which is not being rewritten, so they count as leaked. Harmless once each key is rotated: new key created, stored, all pods confirmed on the new version, then the old key revoked at the provider.
sonnet.q7: Clients no longer copy the key at build time; on every outgoing call the client calls secrets.get("<name>") and puts the value in the Authorization header, so the refreshed key is used from the next request with no restart.
sonnet.q8: After the new version is written, wait for the refresh (at most 5 minutes, allow 10), then check /healthz on every pod; all 4 must show the new version id. Only then does the security on-call revoke the old key.
sonnet.q9: 1) Set store access (and test it), 2) copy keys into the store, 3) one merge: switch app to read from the store and remove api_key lines from config/app.yaml (with CI check), 4) verify, 5) rotate keys at providers one at a time (payments, email, geocoding), 6) retire pre-migration images.
sonnet.q10: From the dev (sandbox) secrets in the store at orders-api/dev/*, with APP_ENV=dev set by make run, using the developer's own login.
sonnet.q11: It does not start with a partial set. It retries the whole load 3 times, 2 seconds apart; if still failing, it logs the error (secret names only) and exits non-zero, never becoming ready.
sonnet.q12: Not decided. Security has not decided whether or how often to rotate on a schedule; the plan covers only the one-time rotation in step 5.
